page: Amazon Web Services c8i.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, configured with 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it lacks GPU acceleration. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2191.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.52 GB/sec. Text processing is a notable strength, placing in the top tier with a Geekbench score of 2958.0. Multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks generally align with average performance tiers; stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is recorded at 8647.04, and the Passmark CPU score is 15544.25. Memory bandwidth tests show 640.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 59.81 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the instance achieves a strong text generation speed of 291.25 tokens/sec using a small 135M parameter model, though prompt processing for a medium 7B model averages 69.74 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.2xlarge offers a high-density compute profile with DDR5 memory and advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions for vector and matrix operations. However, the lack of bundled local storage requires external block storage, which may introduce latency and additional resource overhead. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio also limits its suitability for memory-intensive workloads, positioning it as a specialized compute resource where CPU execution speed is prioritized over memory capacity.

This instance is suited for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, text processing pipelines, single-threaded data compression, and lightweight language model inference. It is also applicable for static web serving and database operations that do not require massive in-memory caching.
